title: The Mixed-Up Parcel
markdown:
The sky popped with pinks and golds. Outside Rosie the bunny’s cozy burrow, dewdrops sparkled. Rosie’s nose twitched. This was no ordinary morning. This was a Delivery Day morning.

“Patch. Wake up. It’s happening.”

Patch the puppy tumbled from his basket with a yip, tail thumping like a drum. “Delivery day? Already?”

“Yes.” Rosie hopped from foot to foot. “The Great Giggles Delivery Club is open for business.” She pictured their cart, their badges. “We’ll dash and zoom, bringing happy parcels all over the place.”

A little note fluttered onto Rosie’s nose. A bright blue box, sunshine-yellow ribbon. Something extra special, the note promised.

“Our very first delivery.” Patch took the box gently in his mouth.

“To Bartholomew Badger,” Rosie read. “By the Whispering Willow trees. That’s past Iolo Bear’s den.” Her heart thumped. What if she dropped it? No. Quick and careful.

“Let’s go.” Patch’s ears flapped.

They dashed. Cool crisp air. Birdsong. A blur of fur and paws. Delivery day, delivery day, the rhythm of it in their feet.

“Faster, Patch. We need to be the best delivery team ever.”

They zipped past Mrs. Goose’s pond. Mrs. Goose waddled out, honking. “What’s the big rush, little ones?”

“Delivering a special parcel,” Rosie called, already halfway past. Oops. The pond was house number one. Bartholomew lived much further on. Rosie’s whiskers drooped a second. She puffed her chest. A challenge.

They bounded past Iolo Bear’s big brown den. Iolo was stretching, furry paws wide. “Morning, Rosie. Morning, Patch.”

“Morning, Iolo,” Rosie puffed, not stopping. Oops again. Iolo’s den was house number two. Bartholomew was not there. A tiny prickle of worry. The thrill pushed it away. She imagined Bartholomew’s happy face when the ribbon came off.

They reached the Whispering Willows, leaves rustling like secrets. “Here it is,” Rosie panted, pointing to a small quiet burrow in the roots. “Bartholomew’s house.”

Patch set the parcel down. Rosie nudged it. It didn’t feel quite right. Bartholomew usually had a booming laugh that bounced off trees. This burrow was too quiet. Was that a faint whiff of pond water?

Patch whimpered. “My tummy is rumbling, Rosie.”

“Mine too. Maybe he’s having a very important quiet tea party and can’t be disturbed.”

They peeked. No Bartholomew. A neat empty room. No tea. No booming laugh. Only a dust-mote doing nothing in a sunbeam.

Rosie picked the parcel up again. She sniffed the yellow ribbon. Pond water. And honey.

Their excitement faded into puzzle-solving. “I think we delivered this to the wrong doors.”

Patch’s tail drooped. “Where is Bartholomew?”

“We have to find him. And get this to him. His tummy is probably rumbling too.” The thought of a sad rumbling tummy made Rosie determined. A special surprise ought to arrive at the right place.

They dashed back with new purpose, past Iolo’s den. Iolo sat outside munching a pot of golden honey. “Morning again. Did you forget something? Or leave something for me?”

“Iolo. We thought this was for Bartholomew, but it smells like honey and pond water. Did you see a parcel like this?”

Iolo blinked, snout sticky. “Not mine. Mine was crunchy acorns this morning. This smells rather sweet, though.”

The blue box felt heavier. First delivery for the Great Giggles Delivery Club, and they had mixed the addresses twice. The sun climbed. Bartholomew was still waiting. Mrs. Goose, when they passed the pond the second time, only shook her head, as if rush were a weather she did not enjoy.

Then a quiet sniffle. Behind a mossy rock near the willows, a familiar sad shape: Bartholomew Badger, shoulders drooped, kind face wet.

“Bartholomew,” they cried, rushing.

He looked up, eyes watery. “Hello, Rosie. Hello, Patch. I was so excited for a special surprise parcel today. It never came.”

Rosie’s heart flip-flopped. She held out the box, paws trembling. “We have it. We are so sorry. We took it to Mrs. Goose’s pond, and then to Iolo’s den. We mixed everything up.”

Patch’s ears drooped. “We’re still learning to be super delivery bunnies and puppies.”

Bartholomew looked at the parcel, then at their earnest faces. A tiny smile peeked through. He could smell something delicious. A soft chuckle rumbled. “Pond water and honey? Oh, you two.”

Rosie untied the ribbon. Inside, on soft paper, were three giant honey cakes, each topped with a bright red berry. Sweet scent. Paper crinkle. Bartholomew’s gasp.

“For you.”

His face bloomed into a grin. He took a big happy bite. The sweetness spread, warm and delightful. Crumbs dusted his chin.

“Would you like to share? We can all be the Great Giggles Delivery Club. With Bartholomew’s Best Bites added in.”

Tails wagged, a blur. They sat by the willows and shared the cakes while the leaves whispered and a beetle took a crumb that nobody minded. The sun beamed, chasing leftover sadness. Rosie still felt fizzy, but steadier now, the kind of excitement that reads the address twice, sniffs the ribbon, and still hops.

“Today,” she said, already bouncing, “is going to be a proper Delivery Day.”

And with a grin they raced off with Bartholomew, ready for whatever delicious thing came next. The adventure was just beginning.
